exposure: Low-grade fever vs. normal body temperature
outcome: Umbilical artery cord pH <7.2 and pH <7.05
Enterobacteriaceae isolates in chorioamniotic membrane cultures
cohort: 1796 women with singleton term pregnancies and prolonged rupture of membranes (>12 hours)
finding: Women with prolonged rupture of membranes and low-grade fever had higher rates of cesarean delivery, postpartum endometritis, and neonatal intensive care unit admission compared to those with normal body temperature.
mod_finding: Low-grade fever was independently associated with both postpartum endometritis (OR 9.0, 95% CI 3.7-21.9) and NICU admission (OR 3.2, 95% CI 1.7-6.0).
birth_weight: Neonatal weight <2500 grams was considered in the analysis of NICU admission.
